newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian envoy urged to investigate Timor death.
newsitem.headline: Australian envoy urged to investigate Timor death.

text.p: Australian supporters of the anti-Indonesian resistance movement in East Timor urged Australia's envoy to Jakarta on Thursday to mount an immediate investigation into the death of key resistance leader David Alex.
Ambassador John McCarthy has been on a fact-finding mission in the former Portuguese colony this week and was due on Thursday to arrive in Kupang in neighbouring West Timor.

"We're asking the ambassador to go back and investigate what happened. He could hop on a plane and be back there in an hour," Rob Wesley-Smith, spokesman for Australians for a Free East Timor, told Reuters.

"How can the number two man in the East Timor resistance be shot in the legs and yet die in the tender arms of the Indonesian military?...People who get leg wounds don't usually die. It needs to be investigated."
He said the group was asking the Australian government to contact McCarthy.
East Timor military commander Colonel Slamat Sidabutar said earlier that Alex died on Wednesday night after being wounded and captured in a gunbattle near the second city of Baucau.
Alex was flown to Dili for treatment but Sidabutar said he died while receiving a blood transfusion. Sidabutar said Alex had received two serious gunshot wounds.
Alex was believed to be the second-in-command of about 200 guerrillas from the military wing of the pro-independence Fretilin party.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 after the abrupt departure of its Portuguese colonisers and annexed it the following year in a move never recognised by the United Nations.
At least 35 people have died in various clashes in East Timor since late May, when Indonesia held its general election. Seventeen security force members died in one attack.
